_note: PF-6 part 2b (concept pf-6-staff r2 BR-8; AG-1-30, -31): the representative types and licensing bodies a staff member picks for their licence record in Canada. Source for every type and for the College and the Chambre: IRCC, 'Use of a Representative (IMM 5476)' instructions page, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/application/application-forms-guides/imm5476.html (page modified 2025-12-12; read from the committed copy official-sources/ircc/web-pages/page-imm5476.html, downloaded 2026-10-19), quote: 'Paid representatives are: consultants who are members in good standing of the College of Immigration and Citizenship Consultants (CICC); lawyers and paralegals who are members in good standing of a Canadian provincial or territorial law society, and students-at-law under their supervision; notaries who are members in good standing of the Chambre des notaires du Québec and students-at-law under their supervision.' The page links the College to http://college-ic.ca/ and the Chambre to https://www.cnq.org/en/. The single law societies are named on IRCC's 'authorized' page (#law-societies), which this session could not reach (network refused www.canada.ca, 18 Nov 2026): their names below are Sample until that page and each society's own site are read and dated (question for the tech lead on the PR). The server stores the words as given (1 to 100 characters) and checks no licence: 'We never verify licences.' Legal points: Unconfirmed: no counsel.
